solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Notorious home recognised by many

parts.note: to be home is to be in, not out
widely known, that is famous

explanation.surface: A house that the whole neighbourhood knows for the wrong reasons.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone well known for something bad; they are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: Volunteers to go after one old Greek character

indicators.note: the volunteers are placed following the other letters

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Volunteers following an elderly Greek, as if in a story about veterans.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, the British Army's part-time volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: The ninth letter of the Greek alphabet, a character in that script.

clue.text: Bureaucrats sign to support party

indicators.note: in a down clue the sign sits beneath the party, holding it up

parts.note: a function is a formal social gathering or party
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Officials holding up placards in support of their political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to support' works only in a down entry: the sign is written below the party, as if propping it up.
explanation.definitionFit: Functionaries are officials who carry out routine administrative duties, the same idea as bureaucrats.

clue.text: Cunning politician — I've a call with him arranged

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are set out in a new arrangement, so they are anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone boasting of having fixed up a phone call with a famously scheming statesman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges the letters of I'VE A CALL plus HIM; 'with' just joins the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The Florentine author of The Prince, whose name became a byword for scheming statecraft.

clue.text: Winning sympathy, becomes arrogant

parts.note: a side that is ahead in a match is said to be up
pity is sympathy for another's suffering

explanation.surface: A victor who is shown compassion turns haughty.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppity describes someone self-important and presumptuous, a near synonym of haughty.

clue.text: A very large amount of land here in Kansas I acquired

definitions.text: A very large amount of land

indicators.note: the letters wanted are found inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A boast about buying up a vast estate in the American Midwest.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across kansAS I Acquired; 'here' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest continent is, playfully, a very big amount of land.

clue.text: Who produced Opposition's manifesto? To follow it can be complicated

parts.note: to shadow someone is to follow them closely

indicators.note: the letters of the short phrase are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A political question about who wrote the opposition party's manifesto, and a grumble that it is hard to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complicated' rearranges IT CAN BE into CABINET. In Britain the shadow cabinet is the opposition party's team of spokespeople mirroring government ministers.
explanation.definitionFit: The opposition's front-bench team would draft its policy platform, so the question describes them.

clue.text: Fire-raiser nobbled on stairs

indicators.note: nobbled means tampered with or interfered with, so the letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who started fires being caught and seized on a staircase.
explanation.walkthrough: To nobble, in British slang, is to tamper with or grab someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who deliberately raises fires commits the crime of arson.

clue.text: Livener to take, short

indicators.note: the word for take is cut short by losing its last letter

parts.note: to nick something is to take or steal it

explanation.surface: Advice to have a quick pick-me-up, a short drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic is something that invigorates or refreshes, which is what a livener does.

clue.text: Trees in area of East London, and South

parts.note: Poplar is a district in the East End of London

explanation.surface: A note about the trees found in a part of East London and in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: POPLAR is a district of East London, near Canary Wharf.
explanation.definitionFit: Poplars are tall fast-growing deciduous trees, so they are examples of trees.

clue.text: Dilemma caused by the last word in forecast

indicators.note: the final word of a prayer is placed inside the forecasting verb

parts.note: to forecast is to predict
amen is the word said at the end of a prayer

explanation.surface: A quandary arising because a prediction has the final say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the last word' sounds like a final say, but it is the word that closes a prayer; 'caused by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A predicament is an awkward situation offering no easy choice, much like a dilemma.

clue.text: Feathery stuff from a plant, lots the wind scattered

indicators.note: things scattered are dispersed and jumbled, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Fluffy seeds from a plant blown about in great quantities by a breeze.
explanation.definitionFit: The light fluffy seed tufts of a prickly weed float on the breeze; they are the feathery plant material described.

clue.text: Liking page with charm

parts.note: to charm is to enchant

explanation.surface: Fondness for a pageboy who has a winning manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a fondness or strong taste for something, the same as a liking.

clue.text: Develop spin in absence of leader

indicators.note: the word for spin is used without its first letter

parts.note: to spin round is to revolve

explanation.surface: Political advice that a message must grow and adapt when nobody is in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To evolve is to develop gradually over time; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Field event record set by American

parts.note: a gramophone record is a disc
US stands for United States, so American

explanation.surface: A record in an athletics field event set by an American competitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record' looks like an athletics best, but it is a vinyl disc.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing the heavy plate is an athletics contest held in the field rather than on the track.

clue.text: Respect shown by eastern power in speech

indicators.note: the word for power is taken by how it is spoken, not how it is written

parts.note: steam is a source of power for engines

explanation.surface: Admiration earned by an oriental ruler through his oratory.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold someone in high regard is to esteem or respect them; the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Essayist becharms all, subtly

indicators.note: subtly suggests the letters are artfully reworked into a different order

explanation.surface: A writer of essays who quietly wins over every reader.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the English essayist known for Essays of Elia (1775-1834).
explanation.definitionFit: This Romantic-era writer is best known for his personal essays under the pen name Elia.

clue.text: Soldiers on duty, initially in fix

parts.note: soldiers in the ranks are men

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: Troops on duty find themselves in a tight spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To mend something broken is to fix or repair it.

clue.text: Stupid, a transgression in office at the end

parts.note: a sin is a transgression against moral law

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word before is taken

explanation.surface: A daft misdeed committed by someone in power at the close of their term.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means foolish, literally like an ass, so it is a synonym of stupid.

clue.text: Boy finding any number in lake

indicators.note: the number is put inside the lake

parts.note: Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America
N stands for an unspecified number in algebra

explanation.surface: A lad discovering countless things in a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie is a boy's name, a short form of Ernest.

clue.text: Job in test, as keeper

indicators.note: the letters needed sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A trial assignment given to a goalkeeper or a zookeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across tesT AS Keeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is a piece of work to be done, which is what a job is.

clue.text: Dreadful ad item: it's taken off

indicators.note: something dreadful is in a bad state, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the word it, with the apostrophe s serving as a link meaning has

explanation.surface: A complaint that a terrible advertisement has been withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken off' looks like withdrawn, but it means mimicked; the 's of it's reads as 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to mimic or parody them, so taken off means copied.
